subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 0 easy / 100 medium / 0 hard. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: The crystals seen in gouty arthritis are:
questions.explanation: Gout: needle-shaped, negatively birefringent urate crystals; pseudogout: rhomboid, positively birefringent CPPD crystals with chondrocalcinosis (menisci).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: In concentric contraction, as the velocity of shortening increases, the force the muscle can produce:
questions.explanation: Hill's curve: force falls as shortening velocity rises; eccentric force increases with the speed of lengthening.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: In the first 6–8 weeks of a strength-training programme, the increase in strength is mainly due to:

options.B: Neural adaptations (increased motor unit recruitment and synchronisation)

questions.explanation: Hypertrophy becomes dominant after the first 6–8 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Pelvic floor muscle training is the first-line treatment for:

options.D: Urge incontinence due to an infection only

questions.explanation: Kegel exercises strengthen the levator ani and urethral sphincter; a 3-month programme is recommended.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The hamstring muscles are supplied by the:

options.B: Tibial portion of the sciatic nerve (the short head of biceps by the common peroneal)

questions.explanation: Semitendinosus, semimembranosus and long head of biceps: tibial division; short head of biceps: common peroneal division.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Pain over the lateral epicondyle on resisted wrist extension with the elbow extended and forearm pronated (Cozen's test) indicates:
questions.explanation: Cozen's and Mill's tests stress the common extensor origin (ECRB) to reproduce lateral elbow pain.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The asymmetrical tonic neck reflex (ATNR) consists of:

options.B: Extension of the arm and leg on the face side and flexion on the skull side when the head is turned
options.C: Flexion of the neck on the trunk
options.D: Symmetric flexion of arms and extension of the legs

questions.explanation: ‘Fencer posture’; it should be integrated by 6 months. Obligatory ATNR interferes with rolling and bringing hands to midline.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing is characteristic of occlusion of the:

options.C: Internal carotid at the cavernous sinus

questions.explanation: PCA supplies the occipital lobe; macular sparing occurs because of dual MCA/PCA supply at the occipital pole.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: For a very painful, irritable joint, the most appropriate Maitland mobilisation is:

options.A: Grade IV at the end of range
options.C: Grade I–II oscillations, within the pain-free range

questions.explanation: Gentle low-grade oscillations stimulate mechanoreceptors and inhibit pain (gate control) without provoking the irritable tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The Grotthus–Draper law states that:

options.A: Radiation intensity falls with the square of the distance
options.B: Metabolic rate doubles for each 10 °C rise
options.C: Only radiation that is absorbed by the tissue can produce an effect in it
options.D: Heat produced is proportional to I²Rt

questions.explanation: For any physiological effect, radiation must be absorbed; reflected or transmitted radiation produces no effect.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The minimum and maximum scores on the Glasgow Coma Scale are:
questions.explanation: GCS = eye (1–4) + verbal (1–5) + motor (1–6) = 3–15; ≤8 is severe brain injury.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The FABER (Patrick's) test assesses the:
questions.explanation: Flexion, abduction and external rotation of the hip stress the hip and SI joint; groin pain indicates hip pathology, posterior pain the SI joint.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The classic faradic-type current used to stimulate normal innervated muscle consists of:

options.B: Short-duration (<1 ms) pulses repeated at about 50–100 per second
options.C: Long-duration pulses (>100 ms) repeated once per second

questions.explanation: Faradic-type current uses short pulses to stimulate the motor nerve, producing tetanic contraction at 50–100 Hz. It is unsuitable for denervated muscle.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Hughston's posteromedial drawer sign is performed with the patient supine, knee flexed 80-90°, hip flexed 45°, and the foot slightly medially rotated. A positive test (excessive posterior movement/rotation of the medial tibia) is most indicative of injury to which primary structure?

options.B: Posterior cruciate ligament (along with posteromedial supporting structures)

questions.explanation: A positive Hughston's posteromedial drawer sign indicates injury to the posterior cruciate ligament, along with possible involvement of the posterior oblique ligament, medial collateral ligament, semimembranosus, and posteromedial capsule — it tests for posteromedial rotary instability of the knee.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Ligament Stability, Posteromedial and Posterolateral Drawer Sign
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: In leprosy, nerve abscess is most often seen in the:
questions.explanation: Thickened ulnar, common peroneal, great auricular and median nerves are typical; claw hand and foot drop result.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The earliest lesion of atherosclerosis is the:
questions.explanation: Lipid-laden foam cells in the intima.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Dupuytren's contracture is MOST commonly associated with:

options.D: Alcoholic cirrhosis, diabetes and epilepsy treated with phenytoin

questions.explanation: Commonest in middle-aged men of Northern European descent; ring finger most affected.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: In psoriasis the epidermal transit time is shortened to about:
questions.explanation: Normal epidermal turnover takes about 28 days (up to 70 including full migration); in psoriasis it is greatly accelerated; UV reduces cell proliferation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Exercise recommended for osteoporosis includes:

options.A: Weight-bearing and resistance exercise with avoidance of forceful spinal flexion

questions.explanation: Weight-bearing exercise maintains bone density; avoid loaded flexion and rotation that increase vertebral fracture risk.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Down syndrome is most commonly due to:
questions.explanation: Associated with advanced maternal age, congenital heart disease (AV canal defect) and early Alzheimer's.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Flat foot (pes planus) in a toddler is usually:

options.C: Physiological and resolves as the arch develops

questions.explanation: The medial arch develops by 6–10 years; painful rigid flat foot suggests tarsal coalition.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The World Health Organization defines a 'zoonosis' as:

options.A: Any infection that only ever affects animals, never humans
options.B: A disease or infection that is naturally transmissible from vertebrate animals to humans
options.C: An infection transmitted exclusively via insect vectors
options.D: A disease found only in tropical climates

questions.explanation: The WHO defines a zoonosis as a disease or infection naturally transmissible from vertebrate animals to humans. Infected animals may be asymptomatic, and some zoonoses (e.g. Q fever, Ebola) can then spread onward between humans, causing secondary disease.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Epidemiology of Infection — Reservoirs of Infection
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Night vision (scotopic vision) is mediated by:
questions.explanation: Cones mediate colour vision and visual acuity in daylight; rhodopsin needs vitamin A.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Exercise-induced bronchospasm is best prevented by:

options.C: Warm-up, a pre-exercise inhaled bronchodilator and breathing through the nose in warm humid air

questions.explanation: Cold, dry air is a trigger; a gradual warm-up and prophylactic β2-agonists help.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The ulnar nerve supplies:

options.A: Flexor carpi ulnaris, medial half of flexor digitorum profundus, hypothenar muscles, interossei and adductor pollicis

questions.explanation: It passes behind the medial epicondyle (the ‘funny bone’).
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The medial meniscus is injured more commonly than the lateral meniscus because it is:

options.B: Less mobile, being attached to the medial collateral ligament and joint capsule

questions.explanation: The medial meniscus is firmly attached to the deep MCL and capsule, so it is less able to move away from compression and rotation forces.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Cauda equina syndrome presents with:

options.A: Ipsilateral weakness with contralateral pain loss
options.B: Saddle anaesthesia, bladder/bowel dysfunction and flaccid lower limb weakness

questions.explanation: It is a lower motor neurone injury of the lumbosacral roots requiring urgent decompression.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In NYHA class III heart failure the patient:

options.B: Has marked limitation: comfortable at rest but less-than-ordinary activity causes symptoms
options.C: Has no symptoms with ordinary activity

questions.explanation: Class I no limitation; II slight limitation; III marked limitation; IV symptoms at rest.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Massive haemoglobin absorption by the renal tubules in severe falciparum malaria produces which complication?
questions.explanation: In falciparum malaria, massive absorption of haemoglobin (released by destroyed red cells) by the renal tubules produces blackwater fever, also called haemoglobinuric nephrosis.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: For the vertebroscapular muscles (e.g., the rhomboids), resistance is preferably applied on the arm rather than directly on the scapula, their true point of insertion. Why?

options.A: It is simply easier for the therapist to grip the arm
options.B: The longer lever at the arm better reflects the functional demand of controlling the weight of the whole upper limb
options.C: The scapula moves too unpredictably to resist against
options.D: Resistance at the scapula risks skin breakdown

questions.explanation: Applying resistance on the arm uses a longer lever that more closely reflects the functional load these muscles must control (the weight of the arm), rather than testing at their literal anatomical insertion.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels and Worthingham's Muscle Testing, 9th ed.
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 1: Principles of Manual Muscle Testing
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A contrast bath in the upper or lower limb is traditionally applied as:

options.D: About 3–4 minutes of warm immersion alternating with about 1 minute of cold

questions.explanation: Alternating vasodilatation and vasoconstriction (the ‘pump’ effect) is thought to help in subacute oedema and stiffness; the usual ratio is 4:1 hot:cold.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The scapulohumeral rhythm during arm elevation is approximately:

options.A: 2° of glenohumeral motion for every 1° of scapulothoracic motion

questions.explanation: Of 180° elevation, about 120° occurs at the glenohumeral joint and 60° at the scapulothoracic joint (2:1).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Coordination exercises such as Frenkel's are based on the principle of:

options.B: Repetition of controlled movements with visual feedback

questions.explanation: They re-educate smooth, accurate movement in ataxia by progressively increasing complexity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: In an isometric contraction of a muscle:

options.D: Tension increases but muscle length remains constant

questions.explanation: No external work is done.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: In generalised peritonitis the abdominal wall typically shows:

options.A: Board-like rigidity and absent bowel sounds
options.B: Soft, distended abdomen with loud bowel sounds

questions.explanation: Rebound tenderness and guarding indicate peritoneal irritation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: In fracture healing, the stage in which a soft callus forms from fibrocartilage is the:
questions.explanation: Sequence: haematoma/inflammation → soft callus → hard callus → remodelling.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Damage to Wernicke's area, located in the left temporal lobe, characteristically produces speech that is:

options.A: Completely absent — the patient cannot make any sound
options.B: Fluent in output but conveying little actual meaning, with impaired understanding of speech and written language
options.C: Slow and effortful but perfectly meaningful
options.D: Normal in every respect except pitch

questions.explanation: Wernicke's area damage markedly impairs comprehension of spoken and written language. Characteristically, the patient's own speech remains fluent in its flow and rhythm but conveys little coherent meaning.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Biology of Behavior — Temporal-Lobe Association Cortex, Language Functions
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: Interrupted direct current of long pulse duration is used mainly to stimulate:

options.A: Nerve roots for pain gate control

questions.explanation: Denervated muscle has a higher chronaxie and needs long-duration pulses (tens to hundreds of ms) of adequate intensity to contract.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Rehabilitation of a person who has lost a limb to enable return to productive work is:
questions.explanation: Vocational rehabilitation includes assessment, training, placement and follow-up.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: A neuropathic (Charcot) joint is typically:

options.A: Associated with severe pain at rest

questions.explanation: Loss of pain/proprioception leads to repeated trauma; most common cause is diabetes (foot/ankle); also syphilis, syringomyelia, leprosy.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which postnatal exercise is recommended to help restore pelvic floor function?

options.B: Pelvic floor (Kegel) contractions starting within the first days after delivery

questions.explanation: Also deep abdominal (transversus) activation and gradual return to activity.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: High-voltage pulsed current (HVPC) is best described as:

options.A: A symmetrical biphasic square wave of long duration
options.B: A continuous direct current of low voltage
options.C: A twin-peak, monophasic pulse of very short duration with a low average current

questions.explanation: HVPC has a very high peak voltage (>150 V) but very short pulses (about 5–20 µs), so the average current is small and comfortable; it is used for oedema, wound healing and pain.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In the acute stage of GBS, physiotherapy emphasises:

options.A: Heavy resistance exercise to build strength
options.B: Prolonged electrical stimulation with high intensity
options.D: Respiratory care, positioning, passive movements and preventing contractures, avoiding fatigue

questions.explanation: Monitor vital capacity and respiratory function; overwork weakness is a risk; gentle exercise progresses gradually.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Testing the medial hamstrings in prone requires the hip to be:

options.A: Laterally rotated with the knee extended
options.B: Slightly medially rotated with the knee flexed, resistance on the distal leg

questions.explanation: Medial rotation of the hip with knee flexion isolates semitendinosus and semimembranosus; lateral rotation emphasises biceps femoris.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: After prolonged immobilisation, the strength of ligaments:

options.B: Decreases due to loss of collagen and weak cross-link formation

questions.explanation: Ligament insertion sites weaken fastest; recovery takes much longer than the immobilisation period.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Which hormone is chiefly responsible for the 'milk ejection' or 'let-down' reflex during breastfeeding?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is the major galactokinetic hormone: suckling triggers a neural reflex arc to the hypothalamus, causing oxytocin release from the posterior pituitary, which contracts the myoepithelial cells around the alveoli and ducts, forcing milk down into the lactiferous ducts (the 'let-down' reflex). Prolactin, by contrast, drives milk secretion itself (lactogenesis/galactopoiesis), not its ejection.
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.sourceChapter: Normal Puerperium — Physiology of Lactation, Galactokinesis
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Peripheral neuropathy caused by isoniazid is prevented by supplementing:
questions.explanation: Isoniazid also causes hepatotoxicity.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: In behavioural treatment of anorexia nervosa aimed at weight gain, what is the recommended maximum safe rate of weight gain?

options.C: There is no upper limit — faster is always better

questions.explanation: Weight gain in anorexia nervosa treatment should not exceed 1.5 to 2 kg per fortnight — too-rapid weight gain is considered neither desirable nor safe, and patients are often encouraged to eat smaller, more frequent meals (around six per day) rather than large ones.
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: What is the key limitation of Sanger's reagent (1-fluoro-2,4-dinitrobenzene) compared to Edman's reagent for determining a protein's amino acid sequence?

options.A: It only works on carbohydrates, not proteins
options.B: After labelling the N-terminal residue, the protein must be fully hydrolysed to identify it — destroying the polypeptide and preventing repeated sequencing cycles
options.C: It cannot label any amino acid at all
options.D: It is more expensive but otherwise functionally identical to Edman's reagent

questions.explanation: Sanger's reagent labels the free N-terminal amino group, but identifying that labelled residue requires complete hydrolysis of the protein — destroying it in the process. This makes it useful only for identifying the N-terminal residue once, unlike Edman degradation which can be repeated.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.sourceChapter: Proteins and Amino Acids — Determination of Primary Structure
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: A daily, chronic productive cough is described as a fundamental feature of which conditions?
questions.explanation: A chronic productive cough occurring every day is a fundamental feature of chronic bronchitis and bronchiectasis, whereas interstitial lung disease is characteristically associated with a persistent DRY cough.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The correct sequence of a normal cough is:

options.B: Deep inspiration, glottis closure with raised intrathoracic pressure, then forced expiration with glottis opening

questions.explanation: Inspiration, compression (glottic closure + contraction of expiratory muscles), expulsion.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: On the ASIA Impairment Scale, a complete injury (no sensory or motor function in S4–S5) is graded:
questions.explanation: A complete; B sensory incomplete; C motor incomplete (more than half key muscles <3); D motor incomplete (≥ half ≥3); E normal.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Haemophilia A is due to deficiency of factor:
questions.explanation: X-linked recessive; haemarthrosis is the hallmark; avoid intramuscular injections.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Excessive femoral anteversion is associated with:
questions.explanation: The normal anteversion angle in adults is about 15°; excess causes in-toeing, patellar squint and increased hip medial rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Corticosteroid use weakening host defence mechanisms and allowing reactivation of latent tuberculosis is an example of which category of adverse drug effect?

options.B: A secondary effect (an indirect consequence of the drug's primary action)

questions.explanation: Secondary effects are indirect consequences of a drug's primary action — corticosteroids' primary immunosuppressive action indirectly allows latent infections like tuberculosis to reactivate, and similarly, tetracyclines suppressing normal bacterial flora can indirectly permit superinfections.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: The obturator nerve supplies:
questions.explanation: Passes through the obturator canal; also gives cutaneous supply to the medial thigh.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Which walking aid provides the greatest base of support and stability?
questions.explanation: A walker supports up to 50% of body weight and is used when balance is poor.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The force of friction between two surfaces is proportional to:

options.C: The normal (perpendicular) force pressing them together and the coefficient of friction

questions.explanation: F = μN; it opposes sliding and is relevant to gait and walking aids.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The most effective single intervention to reduce falls in older adults is:

options.D: Multicomponent exercise including balance and strength training

questions.explanation: Tai chi, Otago and balance training reduce fall rate by ~25–40%; also assess home hazards and medication.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A burn destroying the entire epidermis and dermis with damage to subcutaneous tissue is classified as:
questions.explanation: Full-thickness burns are painless, leathery and need grafting.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A swan-neck deformity of the finger consists of:
questions.explanation: Common in rheumatoid arthritis; volar plate laxity at the PIP joint and tight intrinsics produce PIP hyperextension with DIP flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which of the following is described as a powerful, independent risk factor for stroke, associated with roughly a fivefold increase in risk?
questions.explanation: Atrial fibrillation is described as a powerful risk factor for stroke, associated with approximately a fivefold increase in stroke risk, due to its potential to generate cardiac emboli.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan, Physical Rehabilitation
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 15: Stroke — Risk Factors and Stroke Prevention
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In patients with hypertension, which type of exercise should be limited?
questions.explanation: Isometric effort and breath-holding cause marked rises in blood pressure; dynamic aerobic exercise lowers resting BP.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: According to Lambert's cosine law, absorption of radiation at a surface is maximal when the rays strike it:

options.D: At right angles (perpendicular) to the surface

questions.explanation: Maximum intensity is received when the beam is perpendicular to the surface; reduces with the cosine of the angle of incidence.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Orchidopexy for a palpable undescended testis is ideally performed at what age, to optimise fertility outcomes?

options.D: Age has no bearing on fertility outcomes

questions.explanation: Orchidopexy is ideally performed as a day-case procedure between 6 and 12 months of age. Bringing the testis into the scrotum (below core body temperature) at a young age optimises spermatogenesis and fertility outcomes.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Paediatric Surgery — Undescended Testes
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The unit of power is the:
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work; 1 watt = 1 joule per second.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A Pearson correlation coefficient of −0.9 indicates:
questions.explanation: r ranges from −1 to +1; r² gives the proportion of variance explained.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The features of nephrotic syndrome are:

options.D: Proteinuria > 3.5 g/day, hypoalbuminaemia, oedema and hyperlipidaemia

questions.explanation: Minimal change disease is the commonest cause in children.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Which enzyme is most specific for myocardial infarction?
questions.explanation: AST/ALT rise in liver disease; amylase/lipase in pancreatitis.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Anaemia in pregnancy is defined as a haemoglobin below:
questions.explanation: Severe anaemia is Hb < 7 g/dL; iron and folic acid supplementation are routine.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Which lung cancer is MOST strongly related to smoking and arises centrally?

options.B: Squamous cell carcinoma and small cell carcinoma

questions.explanation: Adenocarcinoma is the most common type overall and arises peripherally.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: In the acute stage of myositis ossificans, treatment should include:

options.A: Rest/immobilisation, avoiding massage and forced passive stretching

questions.explanation: Forced stretching and massage aggravate bleeding and bone formation. Active pain-free movement is introduced only after the acute phase subsides.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Mechanical cervical traction to separate the posterior elements (e.g. facet joints, foramen) is usually applied with the neck positioned in:
questions.explanation: Moderate flexion opens the intervertebral foramina and posterior joints most effectively; extension would compress them.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Standard (universal) precautions in physiotherapy include:

options.A: Wearing a mask for every patient
options.C: Avoiding all treatment of HIV-positive patients
options.D: Hand hygiene, gloves for blood/body fluid contact and safe sharps disposal

questions.explanation: Treat all blood and body fluids as potentially infectious; hand washing is the single most important measure.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A myostatic contracture is due to:

options.B: Fibrosis of the joint capsule only
options.C: Shortening of the muscle without structural changes in the joint

questions.explanation: Myostatic contractures result from prolonged positioning with the muscle shortened and respond to stretching, whereas pseudomyostatic contractures are due to CNS lesions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Nasal cannula oxygen at 2–4 L/min delivers approximately:
questions.explanation: Each litre adds about 4% over the 21% in room air; flows above 4 L/min dry the nasal mucosa.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: In the long bones of the upper limb, the 'growing ends' (which fuse with the shaft latest) are located at which joints?

options.D: All joints fuse at exactly the same time

questions.explanation: By the law of ossification, the epiphysis that appears first at a given end fuses last. In the upper limb this means the upper end of the humerus and the lower ends of both the radius and ulna are the 'growing ends' — they fuse with their shafts later than the corresponding opposite ends.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Upper Limb
questions.sourceChapter: Bones of the Upper Limb — Ossification
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.topic: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle
questions.question: In a practical setup for stimulating the quadriceps with a faradic-type current, where is the indifferent (larger) electrode typically placed, per Clayton's described technique?

options.A: Over the femoral nerve in the femoral triangle
options.B: Directly over the motor points of the quadriceps only, with no separate indifferent electrode

questions.explanation: In the classic technique for faradic stimulation of the quadriceps, one electrode and pad is placed over the femoral nerve in the femoral triangle and secured with a sandbag or bandage, while the other (active) electrode pad is placed across the motor points of the quadriceps.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Tinel's sign is elicited by:

options.C: Percussing over a nerve to produce tingling in its distribution

questions.explanation: A positive Tinel's (distal tingling on percussion) marks a regenerating nerve front or a compressed nerve (e.g. carpal tunnel).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The energy absorbed or released when a substance changes state without a change in temperature is called:
questions.explanation: Latent heat is the energy needed for a change of state (e.g. water to vapour); it explains the cooling effect of vapocoolant sprays and evaporation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Occlusion of a posterior cerebral artery (PCA), affecting the occipital lobe, characteristically produces:

options.B: Complete bilateral blindness in every case
options.D: Pure motor weakness with no sensory or visual involvement

questions.explanation: The PCA supplies the occipital lobe (primary visual cortex); occlusion produces contralateral homonymous hemianopsia. Bilateral PCA occlusion can cause cortical blindness, but this is not the typical single-vessel presentation.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan, Physical Rehabilitation
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 15: Stroke — Posterior Cerebral Artery Syndrome
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The close-packed position of the knee joint is:
questions.explanation: Close-packed (maximum congruency and ligament tension): knee full extension; hip extension with medial rotation; elbow extension; shoulder abduction with lateral rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Degeneration of dopaminergic neurones of the substantia nigra causes:
questions.explanation: Huntington's is caused by degeneration of the caudate nucleus.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂ max) is best described as:

options.A: The amount of oxygen in arterial blood
options.B: The highest rate at which the body can consume oxygen during maximal dynamic exercise

questions.explanation: It is the best measure of aerobic fitness; limited by cardiac output.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Anterior Cerebral Artery (ACA) syndrome classically produces contralateral hemiparesis and sensory loss that is:

options.A: Greater in the lower extremity than the upper extremity
options.B: Greater in the upper extremity and face than the lower extremity
options.C: Equal throughout the whole body with no distinguishing pattern

questions.explanation: Because the ACA supplies the medial aspect of the cerebral hemisphere where the lower extremity is somatotopically represented, ACA syndrome classically produces contralateral hemiparesis and sensory loss with greater involvement of the lower extremity than the upper extremity — the opposite pattern to MCA syndrome.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan, Physical Rehabilitation
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 15: Stroke — Anterior Cerebral Artery Syndrome
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Analysis of variance (ANOVA) is used to compare means of:
questions.explanation: Post-hoc tests (Tukey, Bonferroni) identify which groups differ.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Slipped upper femoral epiphysis typically presents in:

options.A: An obese adolescent boy with hip or referred knee pain

questions.explanation: SUFE occurs at puberty, often overweight; the leg lies externally rotated and shortened. Always examine the hip when a teenager complains of knee pain.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis presents with:

options.B: Haematuria, hypertension and oedema 1–3 weeks after a streptococcal infection

questions.explanation: Low C3 and raised ASO titre.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Which of the following is a facilitatory technique used to increase tone?
questions.explanation: Quick stretch, tapping, brushing, vibration and resistance facilitate muscle activity; slow, rhythmic techniques inhibit.

questions.question: The carpal tunnel contains the median nerve and:

options.C: Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus tendons

questions.explanation: Nine tendons plus the median nerve pass beneath the flexor retinaculum. Ulnar nerve and artery pass in Guyon's canal.

questions.question: Congenital muscular torticollis is due to fibrosis of the:
questions.explanation: The head tilts to the affected side and the chin rotates to the opposite side.

questions.question: Megaloblastic anaemia due to vitamin B12 deficiency can cause:

options.C: Subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord

questions.explanation: Dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts are affected.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Chronaxie is defined as the:

options.A: Longest pulse duration the muscle can tolerate
options.C: Intensity required for a 1 ms pulse
options.D: Shortest pulse duration needed to excite the tissue at an intensity of twice the rheobase

questions.explanation: Chronaxie is a measure of tissue excitability; it is much longer in denervated muscle than in normal innervated muscle.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Exophthalmos and a diffuse goitre in a thyrotoxic patient suggest:
questions.explanation: Caused by TSH receptor-stimulating antibodies.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Back pain that IMPROVES with exercise and worsens with rest, with morning stiffness over 30 minutes in a young male, suggests:
questions.explanation: Inflammatory back pain: onset before 40 years, insidious, morning stiffness, improves with exercise, nocturnal pain.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Reciprocal inhibition means that contraction of an agonist:

options.C: Has no effect on the antagonist

questions.explanation: Basis of agonist-contract stretching techniques.

questions.question: Joule's law states that the heat produced in a conductor is proportional to:

options.B: The voltage divided by the time
options.C: The square of the current, the resistance and the time (I²Rt)
options.D: The square of the resistance and the current

questions.explanation: Heat = I² × R × t. This is why a high-resistance skin interface heats under electrodes and why doubling the current quadruples the heating.

questions.question: Which tool is used to monitor a child's growth and nutrition at the community level?
questions.explanation: Weight-for-age plotting identifies faltering early.

questions.question: Silicosis is caused by inhalation of:
questions.explanation: Byssinosis is due to cotton dust, anthracosis to coal dust, bagassosis to sugarcane fibre.

questions.question: Excess growth hormone in adults causes:
questions.explanation: In children before epiphyseal closure it causes gigantism.
